children: could face substantial legal expenses following Jensen Huang’s departure because its executive liability insurance does not protect the company’s balance sheet, the Financial Times reported, citing people familiar with the coverage.
For investors, the gap raises the possibility that Nvidia
would have to fund certain defense costs and damages itself, adding financial uncertainty to the leadership upheaval. Its shares fell 4.3% Thursday, erasing almost $200 billion in market value.

The chipmaker carries up to $900 million in Side A insurance, which protects directors’ and executives’ personal assets in qualifying cases. Its policy excludes Side B and Side C coverage, which generally protect corporate finances against specified executive-related liabilities and securities claims.
Shareholders have already filed a proposed class action against Nvidia
and Huang, alleging misleading statements about his relationship with Alice Huang, whom U.S. authorities suspect of working for Chinese intelligence. Those allegations have not been established.
